name: Calorie Calculator
author: Md. Zubaer Ahammed

sections.description:
GDPR-ready: Optional privacy consent before storing calculator logs — turn it on under Behaviour, with a customisable consent label.

Calorie Calculator is a free WordPress calorie calculator for fitness, nutrition, health, and coaching sites. Visitors estimate daily calorie needs from age, sex, height, weight, and activity — then see clear BMI, BMR, TDEE, and lose/gain guidelines.

Embed it with a block, shortcode, Elementor widget, or classic sidebar widget. Configure layouts and colours once under Look & feel, then reuse the same calculator across pages.

Results are estimates based on averages. Encourage a balanced diet and sensible activity alongside the numbers.

Why add a calorie calculator?

Interactive tools keep visitors on the page longer and turn curiosity into leads. Optional name and email fields store private Calculator Logs in wp-admin, and Free can notify you or fire a webhook when a log is created.

Science behind the numbers

Free uses the Mifflin–St Jeor equation for basal metabolic rate (BMR), then an activity multiplier for total daily energy expenditure (TDEE / maintain calories). BMI uses height and weight and shows a category label. Results always name the formula used.

What Free results include

  • BMI with category (underweight, normal, overweight, or obese)
  • BMR — calories at rest
  • TDEE — calories to maintain weight for the selected activity level
  • Lose / gain calorie targets (for example 0.5 kg / 1 lb per week)
  • Goal display as lose/gain lines or a single goal dropdown

How to use

  1. Install and activate Calorie Calculator.
  2. Add the Calorie Calculator block, shortcode [calorie_calculator], Elementor widget, or classic widget.
  3. Units default to both US and Metric; you can show only one.
  4. Pick a layout: Modern, Card, Plain HTML (theme-friendly), or Classic — or set a site-wide default under Look & feel.
  5. Optionally show Name and Email fields to store calculator logs.

Using shortcodes

  • Default: [calorie_calculator]
  • In PHP/themes: <?php echo do_shortcode( '[calorie_calculator]' ); ?>
  • Useful Free attributes:
    • unit="usunit/metricunit/both" (default both)
    • template="general/bootstrap-general/plain/old" (omit to use the Look & feel default)
    • show_name_field="true/false" (default true)
    • show_email_field="true/false" (default true)
    • show_firstname_only="true/false" (default false)
    • goal_ui="lines/dropdown" (default follows Behaviour, otherwise lines)
  • Example: [calorie_calculator unit="metricunit" template="general"]

Tip: open Calorie Calculator → Embed for a shortcode builder with live preview and Copy.

Calculator logs

When name and/or email fields are used, submissions can be stored as private Calculator Logs (including BMI and basal BMR). Open Calorie Calculator → Logs to review them. Logs are not publicly queryable.

Look & feel (Free)

Under Calorie Calculator → Look & feel you can:

  • Set the site-wide default layout (Modern, Card, Plain HTML, or Classic)
  • Choose a base font size (small / normal / large)
  • Set primary and alert / error colours (defaults match the Modern teal + yellow brand)

Behaviour (Free)

Under Calorie Calculator → Behaviour you can:

  • Choose the default goal display: lose/gain lines or a single goal dropdown
  • Require a GDPR / privacy consent checkbox before a log is stored (customisable label)
  • Send an outbound webhook (Zapier / Make / n8n Catch Hook) when a log is created
  • Optionally email the admin when a calculator log is stored

Tools (Free)

Under Calorie Calculator → Tools you can:

  • Export / import settings (and restore defaults) for migration or support
  • Copy a system info report for support threads (no secrets)

Pro locked previews

Settings also show locked Pro tabs (Formula & goals, Labels, Integrations, Email, Foods & exercises) so you can preview upgrades without leaving Free. The calculator itself remains fully usable on Free.

Pro version

Calorie Calculator Pro adds PDF download, email results, email-required lead gate, macronutrient breakdown, mailing-list integrations, foods and exercises tables, body fat / Katch–McArdle, Labels overrides, multi-step form flow, and premium support.
sections.installation:
From WordPress.org

  1. In wp-admin go to Plugins → Add New, search for Calorie Calculator, then Install and Activate.
  2. Open Calorie Calculator in the admin menu and review Look & feel and Behaviour (optional).
  3. Add the calculator to any page:
    • Block editor: insert the Calorie Calculator block
    • Shortcode: [calorie_calculator] (or build one under Embed)
    • Elementor: Calorie Calculator widget in the Calorie Calculator category
    • Classic widgets: Appearance → Widgets → Calorie Calculator
  4. Publish the page and test on the front end.

Manual zip upload

  1. Download the plugin zip from WordPress.org.
  2. Go to Plugins → Add New → Upload Plugin, choose the zip, then Install Now and Activate.
  3. Follow steps 2–4 above.
sections.faq:
What is Calorie Calculator?

A free WordPress plugin that embeds a calorie calculator (block, shortcode, Elementor, or classic widget) so visitors can estimate daily calorie needs and see BMI, BMR, TDEE, and simple lose/gain targets.

How do I add the calculator to a page?

Use the Calorie Calculator block, paste [calorie_calculator], add the Elementor widget, or place the classic widget in a sidebar. The Embed tab can generate a shortcode with a live preview.

On which basis are the values calculated?

Free uses the Mifflin–St Jeor equation for BMR, then an activity factor for TDEE (maintain calories). BMI is calculated from height and weight. Results are estimates, not medical advice.

Does the Free version include BMI, BMR, and TDEE?

Yes. Free results show BMI (with category), basal BMR, and TDEE alongside lose/gain calorie targets. Pro adds extras such as macros, PDF/email delivery, and more formulas.

Is the Free calculator actually usable, or only a Pro teaser?

Free is fully usable for embedding and calculating. Some admin tabs are locked Pro previews so you can see what upgrades unlock — they do not block the Free calculator on the front end.

Can I choose US or Metric units?

Yes. Show US, Metric, or both (default). Set it per shortcode/block/widget with unit="usunit", unit="metricunit", or unit="both".

How do I change colours and layout?

Open Calorie Calculator → Look & feel. Choose Modern, Card, Plain HTML, or Classic, set base font size, and pick primary / alert colours. You can also override layout per shortcode with template.

Can I collect emails or leads with the Free version?

Yes. Optionally show Name and Email fields; submissions can be stored as private Calculator Logs. Under Behaviour you can require GDPR consent, email the admin, and send an outbound webhook (Zapier / Make / n8n).

Is it GDPR-ready?

You can require a privacy consent checkbox before a log is stored, and customise the consent label under Behaviour. Align the wording with your privacy policy.

How do I send calculator leads to Zapier, Make, or n8n?

Under Behaviour, enable the outbound webhook and paste your Catch Hook URL. Free fires when a calculator log is created.

Where are calculator logs stored?

In wp-admin under Calorie Calculator → Logs. They are private (not publicly queryable) and can include BMI and basal BMR when those fields are collected.

Does it work with Elementor?

Yes. Add the Calorie Calculator widget from the Calorie Calculator category in Elementor.

What is the difference between Free and Pro?

Free covers embedding, Mifflin–St Jeor results (BMI / BMR / TDEE / goals), layouts, GDPR consent, webhook, admin email, logs, and settings backup. Pro adds PDF/email results, lead gate, macros, mailing-list integrations, foods & exercises, body fat / Katch–McArdle, Labels, multi-step flow, and premium support. Details: Calorie Calculator Pro.

How do I get support?

Use the WordPress.org support forum. Under Tools (or Support), copy the system info report (no secrets) into your thread to speed up troubleshooting.
